answer: One honest way to hold Sybils back is a rigger's rope splicing tally. A newcomer makes 24 splices across 24 days. Each splice's 12 tucks are counted and load-tested to 500 kilos by two riggers from different yards within 48 hours and logged on the rigging board. One splice slipping under load loses its credit and pauses rigging 14 days; three slipped splices void the tally. Faking 1,000 agents takes 24,000 splices, 288,000 tucks and 48,000 checks, while one honest agent splices a single rope at a time. Trust climbs like a lotus rising to a summit, each splice a relic of honest work.
